discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single electron spins in diamond (NV centres) and their use as quantum sensors
motivation: Wrachtrup and Jelezko first detected the magnetic resonance of a single nitrogen-vacancy spin in diamond optically (1997), then demonstrated coherent control, long room-temperature coherence and spin-photon interfaces for single solid-state spins. Lukin, with collaborators, established the conceptual framework for nanoscale magnetometry with single NV spins (2008) and advanced quantum registers built from electron and nuclear spins. Together these achievements turned an individual quantum system, read out at room temperature, into a rigorously calibrated sensor of magnetic fields, electric fields, temperature and stress with nanometre resolution. This capability now serves physics well beyond quantum optics: imaging of magnetism and current flow in condensed matter, superconductivity under megabar pressures in diamond anvil cells, nuclear magnetic resonance of single molecules, and biology. It is a rare case where a basic test of single-spin quantum measurement has become a widely used measurement tool across physics.
